name: Bharti Airtel Ltd
title: Bharti Airtel Ltd - 532454 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Telecom pricing is still the lever: ARPU Rs.264 with no tariff hike, but capex is rising into data centres and homes FWA churn is hurting quality of adds.

capex.quote: wherever we think that there is a legitimate need for the business in order to step up growth, in order to be competitive or to actually plan some of these newer bets ; as a Company, we will not hold back on capex.

triggers.label: Data centre build to 1 GW
triggers.quote: we are scaling up our data center portfolio as we are building out from the 120 to 130 megawatts, all the way to 1 gigawatt over the next few years

triggers.label: Radio capex moderated
triggers.quote: the radio capex has moderated across the portfolio over the last couple of years.

triggers.label: Postpaid adds 1 million record

summary.headline: Airtel group Q1 FY27 revenue Rs58,500 Cr (+5.7% QoQ), EBITDAaL Rs29,800 Cr at 51% margin; India homes net adds slowed to 473,000 on tighter FWA acquisition quality.
summary.overview: Group consolidated revenue rose about 5.7% sequentially to Rs58,500 Crores, with EBITDAaL of Rs29,800 Crores (+4.2%, 51% margin) and capex of about Rs13,390 Crores. India ex-passive infra grew 3.6% sequentially, while Africa posted 5.7% constant-currency revenue growth. Management flagged a deliberate pullback in FWA acquisition after aggressive low-price adds led to higher churn and weaker cohorts, and a pivot toward fiber. Airtel Money is preparing a London listing in 2H 2026 and Nxtra raised $1bn of funding.

segments.name: India mobile
segments.commentary: Added 3.3 million revenue-earning customers and 5 million smartphone data customers; ARPU Rs264 with one extra day in the quarter. Postpaid push supported by Fast Lane 5G network slicing.

segments.name: India homes
segments.commentary: Net adds of 473,000, a moderation after FWA acquisition quality was tightened; digital TV added 6,000 customers, led by IPTV adoption. Management is pivoting to fiber, with FWA limited to where fiber is not available.

segments.name: India B2B (Airtel Business)
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs5,670 Crores, +3.2% QoQ and nearly +12% YoY, driven by large global connectivity deal wins; digital businesses (cloud, cybersecurity, IoT, CPaaS) grew nearly 6% QoQ.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Constant-currency revenue growth 5.7% QoQ; annualised EBITDA above Rs35,000 Crores. Airtel stake raised to over 79% via an EPS-accretive share swap; Indus expanding into three African markets.

segments.name: Airtel Money / Payments bank / NBFC
segments.commentary: Airtel Money Q1 revenue over $400 million (+26% YoY constant currency), London listing planned 2H 2026. Payments bank 120 million monthly transacting users; NBFC lending live, with loan disbursements over Rs750 Crores per month via Airtel Finance.

segments.name: Data centers (Nxtra) and Airtel Cloud
segments.commentary: Data center market share about 12%, targeting 1 GW from 120-130 MW over next few years; Google contract included. Airtel Cloud has 33 customers after 11 added in the quarter. Nxtra raised $1bn to fund expansion.

guidance_outlook: Management sees mid-term mobile ARPU headroom from upgrades, unlimited-plan migration and postpaid; long-term ARPU growth needs data-charging pricing architecture repair, which management says will not be achieved single-handedly.
Management estimates 4-5% sustained ARPU growth over five to seven years from better price architecture, with no need to change entry-level pricing.
Homes: expects momentum to return as acquisition quality repairs; Hexacom expects both circles to return to old growth rates in the next one to two quarters.
B2B margins expected to trend slightly downward over time as digital mix rises, with faster revenue growth as the key metric.
Airtel does not set ROCE targets and says it will fund growth capex without holding back; Nxtra will need debt and equity, funding route to be decided over time.
capex_capacity: Radio capex has moderated over the last couple of years; majority of capex is going to transport (fiber), which includes homes.
5G standalone capex is modest, being largely a software switch; data center build-out is lumpy and will create a period of rapid capex.

Data centers: ambition of 1 GW from 120-130 MW in the next few years; a couple of hundred MW under construction over the next couple of years, with Mumbai land parcels being finalised for the balance.
Over the last three years, about 139,000 km of fiber deployed; Cloud first-round investment completed across three regions.
Hexacom capex directed to 5G densification, network modernisation, fiberisation and homes/IPTV.
demand_pricing: Africa: tele-density about 45%, smartphone penetration 52%, home broadband penetration only 2%, population about 680 million across 14 countries; market structure typically two to three players with cheap spectrum.
FWA: aggressive low-entry pricing led to round-tripping and poor cohort quality; memory and chipset price inflation challenged FWA economics; management says memory cost impact on fiber is modest.
Hexacom mobile customer base 29 million, net adds about 210,000, smartphone adds 344,000; mobile ARPU Rs259.
B2B wholesale runs at low margins and faces price pressure and messaging shift to WhatsApp; connectivity market grows at low single digits.
International roaming improved from the prior quarter after West Asia disruption, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the strong sequential mobile ARPU improvement, and is it sustainable without a tariff hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited data-consumption upgrades, shift to unlimited plans and postpaid acceleration via Fast Lane; sees reasonable mid-term headroom, with long-term growth needing pricing architecture repair.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India's capex is shifting to AI infrastructure, data centers and subsea, and what is the B2B margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Radio capex has moderated; large spend is on transport and fiber, with a rapid data center build-out. B2B margins are expected to trend slightly down as the digital mix rises, but growth is the key metric.

qa_highlights.question: Will Nxtra's capex be funded externally going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Nxtra will need equity and debt; whether funding comes from Airtel's balance sheet or outside is a decision to be taken over time.

qa_highlights.question: What was the FWA churn and will the pullback materially change growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no churn figure; said acquisition was tightened and month-on-month quality is improving, with focus shifting to fiber and FWA where fiber is not available.

qa_highlights.question: Is there confidence in reaching 1 GW of data center capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: hyperscaler workloads in Mumbai require land parcels being finalised, with the Google contract, a few hundred MW under build, and the rest to be filled by Mumbai land.

qa_highlights.question: Why are homes net adds weaker and what changed in mobile net adds?
qa_highlights.answer: Hexacom: acquisition quality was tightened, causing the slowdown; positive signs include steady postpaid additions. Mobile net adds were affected by seasonal depletion, with more adds expected in the second half.

risks_watch: Homes: whether FWA quality correction reverses in coming quarters, and whether homes net adds recover from 473,000.
Pricing: absence of a tariff hike and the unresolved industry pricing architecture could cap mid-term ARPU.
Capex: step-up for data centers and Nxtra funding (debt/equity) could raise leverage at subsidiary level.
Cost: diesel and memory/chipset price inflation pressure on operating costs and FWA economics.
B2B: conversion timelines for Airtel Cloud and data center deals are long, and the digital mix may dilute margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on group scale, Africa and balance sheet, but candid and cautious on India homes/FWA, acknowledging a short-term acquisition-quality correction. Management was evasive on specific targets such as FWA churn, Africa contribution and ROCE, declining to set numbers.
key_quotes: Africa today resembles India nearly 10 years ago - a large, young and increasingly digital population with meaningful headroom for penetration-led growth
the industry must charge for data consumption. This is paramount for sustained ARPU growth in the longer term.

we are actually doubling down on fiber and the memory prices that have gone up on the fiber side with copper and a little bit on this router is actually modest and we are fine to absorb that into one.
